lesson.title: Solving Linear Inequalities
intro: Solving a linear inequality is similar to solving a linear equation.
You can add, subtract, multiply, or divide both sides by the same number.
If you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, you must reverse the inequality symbol.
The solution to an inequality is often a range of values shown on a number line.

workedExample.aiHint: Solve it like an equation, but remember to reverse the inequality if multiplying or dividing by a negative.

questions.prompt: What is the solution to the inequality \(2m - 4 \le 3(2m + 4)\)?
questions.explanation: Distribute: \(2m - 4 \le 6m + 12\). Subtract \(2m\): \(-4 \le 4m + 12\). Subtract 12: \(-16 \le 4m\). Divide by 4: \(-4 \le m\), which means \(m \ge -4\).

questions.prompt: Which graph is the solution to the inequality \(6.4 - 4x \ge -2.8\)?
questions.explanation: Solve the inequality: \(6.4 - 4x \ge -2.8\). Subtract 6.4: \(-4x \ge -9.2\). Divide by -4 and reverse the inequality: \(x \le 2.3\). The correct graph is choice 4.
